text:
anya: Quick bring-up note — ran full onboarding eval for `vectra-small` quantized to int8 on the miniQA holdout. Seeing a ~3.8% absolute drop in recall@1 and a 2.1% drop in recall@5 vs fp16 baseline. Short summary below.

sahil: can you paste the exact eval command and which dataset split?

anya: eval command: `python ci/eval_embeddings.py --model vectra-small --quant int8 --split holdout-miniqa --k 1,5 --batch 256 --seed 42`

anya: results (aggregated across 10 seeds):
```
metric    | fp16   | int8   | delta
--------------------------------
recall@1  | 0.721  | 0.683  | -0.038
recall@5  | 0.915  | 0.894  | -0.021
silhouette| 0.42   | 0.39   | -0.03
```

lucas: hmm interesting — 3.8% at R@1 is noticeable but not catastrophic. how's cluster purity for positive pairs?

anya: pair-precision@1 drops from 0.76 -> 0.73. UMAPs uploaded to the artifact: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/vectra-miniqa/int8-umap.png

julie: do we see any query-length dependence? short queries often get hit worse with quant noise. can you run stratified by query token count (<=8, 9-32, >32)?

anya: just ran quick stratification (single seed):
```
len_bin | fp16_r@1 | int8_r@1 | delta
<=8     | 0.68     | 0.62     | -0.06
9-32    | 0.75     | 0.72     | -0.03
>32     | 0.73     | 0.71     | -0.02
```

sahil: that suggests short queries degrade more — likely due to reduced embedding resolution on short contexts. can you try asymmetric quant (per-channel) vs per-tensor and report? also what's the L2 norm distribution shift?

anya: running per-channel now, will post numbers in ~20m. L2 means: mean norm fp16=12.3, int8(per-tensor)=11.8, int8(per-channel)=12.1

infra-bot: Deployment scheduled: nightly-eval-runner started job 8673 for `vectra-small` int8-per-channel (logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/8673) :rocket:

lucas: if per-channel restores norm and recall, we can add a quantization rule for models with short-query-heavy workloads. also consider small retrain with quant-aware calibration on short queries.

julie: could we patch the serving pipeline with a fallback rule: if query_len<=8 and top_score<0.7, route to fp16 variant? that'd cost a little but might preserve UX for short queries.

anya: agree — i did a rough sim: routing ~6% of traffic to fp16 would recover ~80% of the R@1 loss for short-query cohort.

sahil: please attach the full eval CSV and config. i'll open a ticket for a focused calibration sweep and add a QA job for stratified recall in the onboarding checklist.

anya: attached artifact links in the job logs + uploaded CSV to /artifacts/vectra-small/int8_evals/recall_stratified.csv

julie: thanks — can you add a short blurb to the model-onboard doc (PR) with recommended default quant: per-channel int8 + short-query fallback? i'll review. :+1:

anya: will do. tagging @product for visibility in case short-query apps need heads-up.

lucas: nice work. next steps: wait for per-channel run, then decide: accept int8-per-channel, or keep fp16 for now and schedule QA calibration.

anya: per-channel run finished: recall@1 = 0.707 (vs fp16 0.721) — delta -0.014, much better. uploading final csv.

sahil: cool, please update the onboarding checklist with the following items:
- run stratified recall by query length
- compare per-tensor vs per-channel quant
- compute norm shift and pair-precision
- UMAP spotcheck for short-query clusters

anya: checklist updated and PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/model-onboard/pull/412

julie: let's keep this thread as the audit trail. thanks everyone. :sparkles:
